content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm seeking advice for a setup using [product_name] modules. We have two facilities, a warehouse and offices, connected by network cables. We want to install a button or panel so that when deliveries arrive, a signal is sent to notify the other building, as items have sometimes gone unnoticed for days. I saw an example with lights and blinds, but the network configuration wasn't clearly explained. In my test, pressing a function button flashes a light via the output, but these are currently wired together. I’d prefer to have a [product_name] operator device at the delivery point and the signal light in the office area, connected only through the network. Is this possible, and if so, how should I set it up? Any guidance is appreciated. Thank you in advance.

You can connect [product_name] controllers and [product_name] operator panels via the network. Expansion modules are only physically and electrically attached to a [product_name] controller—not via network. Ensure the IP addresses of controllers and operator panels are within the same IP range, differing only in the last segment, and use the same subnet mask. The operator panel should be configured with the IP address and subnet mask of the controller it will communicate with, as it can only operate with one controller at a time.

Thanks for the response. I've managed to set it up so it now works using only a [product_name] module and power supply at each location where we need the signal. With our network connections and no other [company_name] modules, everything functions as required.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion focused on implementing network-based signaling between separate areas using [product_name] controllers and operator panels. The main challenge was configuring network communication between components without relying on physical wiring. The user successfully achieved their goal by employing [product_name] modules and power supplies at each site, utilizing existing network infrastructure.
analysis.user_expectations: User anticipates straightforward configuration for networked signaling across building areas using [product_name] controllers and operator panels, with dependable operation and clear guidance for setup over the current network.
